graph.title: I2C between two Arduino Nano Every boards (reader and writer)
graph.source_id: nano33BS_06 – Nano Every I2C communication between two boards
notes: The circuit image shows the boards wired directly with no breadboards drawn, but the parts list includes 2 mini breadboards. I assumed each Nano Every straddles its own mini breadboard: left-side pins in row e of the top bank, right-side pins in row f of the bottom bank, columns 1-15.
Jumper wires, resistors and the 3V3 pull-up connection are placed in rows a-c of the same column strips as the Nano pins.
Only 3 jumper wires are needed (GND, SDA/A4, SCL/A5) even though the manual lists 10. The extra wires are not used.
The image labels pins GND, A5, A4 and 3V. I mapped them to the catalogue ports GND1, A5, A4 and 3V3, all on the same side of the board. The exact GND pin is ambiguous; GND2 would also work.

The two 4.7k pull-ups sit on the reader's breadboard (bb1). The reader's 3V3 strip is the pull-up supply. Resistor r1 goes from A5 (SCL) to 3V3 and r2 from A4 (SDA) to 3V3. The image shows the SCL resistor in teal and the SDA resistor in yellow.
The 3V3 rail is not wired to the writer, which gets its own power over USB. Each board is powered and programmed through its own USB cable.
The resistor value is stored as 4700 ohms. USB cable edges have no ports because the usb-cable catalogue part defines none.
The image has A4 and A5 wires crossing at the pull-up junction. The teal and yellow lines do not connect to each other.

breadboard.name: Solderless breadboard
breadboard.port_rule: Holes are named '<column><bank>.<row>': column 1-30, bank 't' (top half, rows a-e) or 'b' (bottom half, rows f-j), e.g. '12t.c', '7b.h'. The 5 holes of one column-bank are one strip. Power rails: 'tp.<n>', 'tn.<n>', 'bp.<n>', 'bn.<n>' (each rail is one strip).
